items.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: “Somebody wants to talk to you.” It’s Hugo Chavez. She’s dating his son, right. He says, “You’ve got to come down.”

ctx.x: You called it. The power of music. You’ve watched it in Venezuela the difference it made with those kids all of a sudden. I don’t know if you’ve ever seen the video. They run it on “60 Minutes” a couple of times.

It’s awesome. It’s funny, because Naomi Campbell’s like my daughter, 16 years. Mandela’s her grandpoppy. I’m poppy. She’s the sweetest girl in the world, but boy, she can do it. She’s always into something. “Poppy” – she’s a writer now, one of the editorial staff for GQ. “Poppy.” “Yes baby?” “Somebody wants to talk to you.” It’s Hugo Chavez. She’s dating his son, right. He says, “You’ve got to come down.” I met Castro at

Birdland two weeks after the revolution. Pee Wee Marquette – he’s staying at the Theresa – Pee Wee Marquette said, “Hey, you all better not mess with me. Better tip me more, because Castro said when the atomic bomb comes in, they’re not going to hit the Theresa Hotel.” Castro was a nice guy then.
